verdict.rationale: Foreloop documents an end-to-end loop: a plain-language request becomes approved tasks, and an agent (Claude Code or Codex) running in your checkout claims a task, does the work and opens a pull request. Intention status also tracks whether the deliverables were actually completed. However, the coding itself is done by an external agent the user runs, and nothing in the pack says tests are written. Missing for 10: any evidence that the agent writes tests, first-party proof of implementation quality beyond task orchestration, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have an agent implement a requested feature end-to-end, including writing tests

citations.quote: That agent asks Foreloop for approved tasks in that repository, claims one, does the work, and opens a pull request from your GitHub account.
"Users can't tell which invoices are overdue" is enough to start; you do not need to know which files change.
The agent then checks Foreloop for approved tasks on a cadence and works them as they arrive.
Each task contract carries the relevant skills into the run, so an agent starts with your team's expectations rather than being corrected afterwards.
